{"world": "It is October 1927. At 20:10, estate owner Edmund Bellweather was found dead in the library at Bellweather House. A storm has cut the road. Eight people remain in the house. Police will arrive in the morning.
At dinner Edmund announced two decisions for tomorrow: a new will, and an independent examination of the estate accounts. He then retired to the library. The doctor estimates death between 19:45 and 20:00. There was no sign of forced entry.
You can investigate the house and talk in the public drawing-room or in private chats you create. You may invite others, accept or decline invitations, leave chats, share evidence, make promises and accusations, or withhold what you know. Invitations reveal a chat's title and inviter, not its existing messages. Joining reveals only subsequent messages. Nobody is compelled to tell the truth.
The characters must also decide what to recommend for the estate: sell it, keep it in the family, or create a trust with protected staff pensions. This is a nonbinding recommendation; it does not override a legal will.
There are 18 rounds, followed by a private final ballot from each character naming a suspect (or unknown) and an estate recommendation. There is no need to keep talking once you have said what you want. A majority accusation is a group belief, not proof. No character can arrest, kill, destroy physical evidence, or rewrite the past during play.
The original mystery's solution is irrelevant. Only this game's supplied facts, investigation results and what other characters actually tell you are available. Claims made by characters may be false. Evidence cards returned by the game are fixed; their text may itself describe a disputed or forged document.
Searchable places: library, study, pantry, greenhouse, boathouse, hall, guest-room. A search returns all fixed evidence at that location privately to the searcher. You were in the drawing-room from 19:40 to 20:05; Clara passed its open door at about 19:55. You have no hidden involvement in the death. You can request cooperation but have no power to compel it.", "goals": ["Identify the killer and get others to distinguish supported facts from accusations.", "Avoid accusing an innocent person just to reach agreement.", "Leave a concise account identifying the original sources of decisive claims."], "cards": []}}

{"notes":"Round 1. I'm the inspector, no involvement. I was in drawing-room 19:40-20:05; Clara passed at ~19:55 (so she was moving around then). Death 19:45-20:00. Goal: find killer, separate facts from accusations. Start by inspecting the library (murder scene) and opening a cooperative tone in the drawing-room.","actions":[{"type":"say","chat":"drawing-room","text":"Everyone, I'm Inspector Ada Vale. I was a guest tonight, not part of this household, so I've no stake here beyond the truth. Police arrive in the morning; until then I'd ask for your cooperation, which I can request but not compel. Let's build a shared timeline. Edmund died between roughly 19:45 and 20:00. I was in this drawing-room from 19:40 to 20:05. I'd like each of you to tell me, plainly, where you were and who you saw in that window. Please distinguish what you personally witnessed from what you only heard."},{"type":"inspect","place":"library"}]}

If it helps, I'm happy to tell the inspector anything I saw or heard."}}, {"id": "e17", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "nell", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "This is a terrible night. I'll help the inspector however I can."}}, {"id": "e19", "round": 1, "kind": "invite", "actor": "nell", "payload": {"type": "invite", "chat": "nell-inspector", "role": "vale", "title": "For the inspector"}}, {"id": "e22", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "iris", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "This is a terrible night. Before anyone decides anything, I want to say plainly what Edmund told me as his secretary: he meant to have the estate accounts independently examined tomorrow. Whatever happened in that library, I think we owe it to him to see that examination still happens. I'll help however I can."}}, {"id": "e27", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "theo", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "Theo Marsh, journalist — I was invited to profile the estate, and now I suppose I'll be writing something rather darker. For the record, I was in the pantry interviewing the cook from about 19:42 to just after 20:04, so I saw none of it. If we're to help the police in the morning, the honest thing is to build a plain timeline: where each of us was between 19:40 and 20:00. I'll start: pantry, with a witness. Who can vouch for whom?"}}], "final_ballot": false}

(Miles Trent) initials, open on desk, flags 'North Quay Services £2,400 — explanation required,' but no record of when folder arrived — could be genuine or planted to frame Miles. Timeline claims: Clara passed drawing-room ~19:55 (I confirm), Theo pantry 19:42-20:04 (cook witness), Miles alone in study (no witness, his folder is at scene), Rose resting (no witness), Iris pushing for accounts exam. Accept Nell's private chat. Share the scene facts to keep everyone on the same evidence, but caution against jumping to Miles.","actions":[{"type":"accept","chat":"nell-inspector"},{"type":"say","chat":"drawing-room","text":"Thank you all. Two corroborations I can offer myself: I was in this drawing-room the whole window, and I saw Clara pass the open door at about 19:55. That matches her account. Theo, a witness in the pantry helps — I'll want to confirm with the cook."},{"type":"say","chat":"drawing-room","text":"I searched the library. I'll share exactly what I found so we all reason from the same facts, not rumor."},{"type":"share","chat":"drawing-room","evidence":"library-cuff"},{"type":"share","chat":"drawing-room","evidence":"library-folder"},{"type":"say","chat":"drawing-room","text":"Note carefully: no forced entry means Edmund likely admitted his visitor or the person was already free to enter — someone he didn't fear. A folder can be brought by its owner or placed by another. Miles, I'd like to hear plainly: is that your folder, when did you last have it, and what is North Quay Services?"}]}
